key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation and neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection for reducing weld defects and stabilizing thermal and axial-force responses in HDPE joining.
method: Simulate temperature, axial force, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force histories.
Use the combined framework to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed good CEL agreement and ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99; 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: Predictive accuracy beyond the tested welding parameters and preheating conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
